html:
The Siege of Szigetvár was the Ottoman siege of a small fortress in southern Hungary in August and September 1566. Its few thousand defenders were led by Nikola Zrinski, to Hungarians Miklós Zrínyi.

Suleiman the Magnificent, on his way to Vienna, stopped to take it. After a month of assaults the defenders were left in the inner castle, and on 8 September Zrinski led the survivors in a final charge and was killed. Suleiman himself had died in his tent days before, a secret kept from the troops. The losses and his death ended the campaign. The siege became a hero tale for both Croatians and Hungarians; Zrinski's great grandson, also Miklós Zrínyi, wrote an epic about it.
